name: Texas Children's Medicaid
description: Free health coverage for children under 19. Income limits are TIERED by the child's age (schema stores the base ceiling): infants under 1 qualify up to 198% FPL, ages 1-5 up to 144% FPL, ages 6-18 up to 133% FPL — each plus a 5% MAGI disregard. The matcher should use children_ages from the profile to pick the right tier; the 133% stored here is the conservative floor.
documents_needed: Child's Social Security number or immigration documents
source: Texas HHSC Texas Works Handbook C-131 (eff. March 2026)

name: Texas CHIP (Children's Health Insurance Program)
description: Low-cost coverage for children under 19 whose family income is too high for Children's Medicaid but at or below 201% FPL. Requires the child to be UNINSURED — matcher must check insurance_status. Enrollment fee up to $50/family/year plus small copays. Designed to catch the 133-201% FPL band where Children's Medicaid ends.
documents_needed: Child's Social Security number or immigration documents
source: Texas HHSC Texas Works Handbook C-131 (eff. March 2026)

name: Texas Medicaid for Pregnant Women
description: Full Medicaid coverage during pregnancy and 12 months postpartum at up to 198% FPL. Notably generous relative to Texas's otherwise strict adult Medicaid — a key match for expecting mothers. Covers prenatal care, delivery, and postpartum care.
source: Texas HHSC Texas Works Handbook C-131 (eff. March 2026)

name: CHIP Perinatal (Texas)
description: Prenatal care and delivery coverage for the unborn child of pregnant people up to 202% FPL who do NOT qualify for Medicaid — including because of immigration status. The key pathway for non-citizen expecting mothers; pair with tx_emergency_medicaid for the delivery itself.
source: Texas HHSC Texas Works Handbook C-131 (eff. March 2026)

name: Texas Medicaid for Parents & Caretaker Relatives
description: Medicaid for parents/caretakers of a dependent child — but Texas has NOT expanded Medicaid, so the income ceiling is extremely low (roughly 16% FPL, only a few hundred dollars a month). Treat matches as low confidence and always note that most childless adults and most working parents do NOT qualify in Texas. The ACA marketplace (100%+ FPL) is the fallback.
documents_needed: Proof of relationship to dependent child
source: Texas HHSC; KFF Medicaid eligibility limits (Jan 2026)

name: Texas Emergency Medicaid
description: Medicaid coverage for emergency medical conditions (including labor and delivery) for people who meet Medicaid rules except for immigration status. The safety net for non-citizens — pair with CHIP Perinatal for prenatal coverage. Covers the emergency condition only, not ongoing care.
documents_needed: Emergency medical documentation from a provider

name: Texas Medicaid for the Elderly & People with Disabilities
description: Medicaid for Texans who are 65+, blind, or disabled, at SSI-level income (~75% FPL for an individual) with resources under $2,000 ($3,000 for couples). SSI recipients are enrolled automatically. Community-based long-term care waivers have separate, higher limits.
documents_needed: Proof of age or disability determination

name: CEAP — Comprehensive Energy Assistance Program (Texas LIHEAP)
description: Help paying electricity and gas bills (up to 6 months for non-vulnerable households, longer for elderly/disabled households), plus crisis assistance and HVAC repair. Income at or below 150% FPL; categorical eligibility for households receiving SNAP, TANF, or SSI. Administered by local subrecipients in all 254 Texas counties.
documents_needed: Proof of household income for all members

name: Texas TANF Cash Assistance
description: Monthly cash help for families with children 18 or younger — but Texas limits are among the lowest in the country. The recognizable-needs screen is ~$188/month for a one-parent family of three (~8% FPL), so only families in deep poverty pass. Max grant $382/month for that family. Requires children; 'child-only' cases (relative caregivers of a child) have their own track and are worth flagging to grandparents/kinship caregivers.
documents_needed: Proof of children in the household
source: Texas HHSC Texas Works Handbook C-110/C-111 (rev. Oct 2025)

name: Texas Unemployment Benefits (TWC)
description: Weekly payments for workers who lost their job through no fault of their own. Not poverty-tested — eligibility is based on wage history during the base period. Matcher should key on employment_status 'recently_unemployed' or 'unemployed', not the FPL field. Average benefit replaces roughly half of prior wages, capped at ~$577/week.
documents_needed: Work history for the last 18 months
